$comment: Works withheld from the site, one entry per work id.
WHAT THIS IS ACTUALLY FOR: quality. A work whose parse is damaged — text
missing, paragraphs swallowed by a source-HTML defect — is worse than a
work we don't publish at all, because a reader has no way to tell that
what they are reading is incomplete. Withholding it and pointing at
vatican.va is honest; shipping a document with 40% of its paragraphs
silently absent is not. Entries here are expected to be TEMPORARY: the
fix is to repair the parser and remove the entry.
It also serves the rights case ('kind': 'rights'), but that is the lesser
use and this mechanism does not really solve it — see the note at the end.
FIELDS:
kind    'quality' (default) or 'rights'. Chooses which notice the reader
sees. Don't use one for the other: the page tells the reader
which it is, and being wrong about that is worse than silence.
date    ISO date the work was withheld.
reason  Free text, shown to the reader verbatim. Be specific — 'missing
~41% of its paragraphs to the source-HTML defect in
docs/research/vatican-documents.md §7.1' is useful to a reader
deciding whether to trust us; 'quality issues' is not.
WHAT AN ENTRY DOES: everything derived from the work stops being written
into the build — reading text AND structure tree (scripts/sync-corpus.mjs).
For a quality withholding that is exactly right: a table of contents built
from a broken parse is broken too. Only the manifest survives, which is
enough for the work's page to name it, explain, and link to vatican.va.
Listings mark the work rather than hiding it, so it stays findable and
nobody 'fixes' its absence.
Keyed by WORK ID ('encyclical.humanae-vitae.pt'), not slug, because parse
damage is usually per-edition: a document's PT edition can be broken while
its EN one is clean, and withholding both would throw away a good text to
hide a bad one.
WHAT BREAKS: per-section URLs (/documents/{slug}/{n}) stop being generated,
since the structure they are enumerated from is gone, so an external
bookmark to a section lands on the site's 404 rather than on the notice.
Links from inside the site do NOT break — refs.ts asks
documentSectionExists before linking, so citations quietly stop linking
rather than pointing at nothing, and the build stays green under
prerender's handleHttpError: 'fail'.
ON THE RIGHTS CASE, HONESTLY: this is per-work, and a takedown from the
Holy See would not be. Essentially the whole corpus outside the two Bible
editions is Libreria Editrice Vaticana material, so such a request would
concern most of the site at once — a whole-site decision (stop publishing,
or degrade everything to link-outs), not a handful of entries here. This
file is not that lever and should not be mistaken for one. See
docs/decisions.md, 2026-08-16.
Example:
"encyclical.humanae-vitae.pt": {
"kind": "quality",
"reason": "Missing ~41% of its paragraphs to the source-HTML defect in docs/research/vatican-documents.md §7.1."

encyclical.pascendi-dominici-gregis.pt.reason: Our parse of this edition captured no paragraphs at all — the source page's markup defeated it. Diagnosed per work in the corpus manifest's own notes.
